source_notes: Scaffold: Kiwoom Securities '병목의 확산' bottleneck-propagation chart (11 rungs), transcribed in _reference_kiwoom_bottleneck_map.md. Used for layer completeness, NOT as evidence.

Layers absent from the Kiwoom chart were added by chain-tracing: EDA/IP, wafers & compound substrates, photomask, probe cards & sockets, subfab components, process chemicals, package-level thermal, specialty foundry, and the jurisdiction layer.
All tickers here are pipeline-verified as priceable via serenity_pipeline.py discover on 2026-07-26. NO financial figures are stored in this file — numbers expire; run the pipeline.

SEC EDGAR returned HTTP 403 for every request from this environment on 2026-07-26 (retried with explicit identity, and outside the sandbox). Filing-derived facts — customer concentration %, country revenue %, financing structure — were therefore UNAVAILABLE this session. Any 'link' marked CONFIRMED below rests on a company press release, conference disclosure, or a cited third-party source, never on a filing read this session.

Foreign winners are named honestly and resolved down the US-listed ladder. OTC lines (SIVEF, SLOIF, LPKFF, IQEPF, XFABF) were confirmed to price on 2026-07-26, but OTC liquidity and spreads are a real execution constraint, not a footnote.

layers.name: AI accelerators — merchant GPU and custom ASIC/XPU
layers.bottleneck_mechanism: Not the die itself any more. Supply is gated by simultaneous access to leading-edge wafer starts, HBM stacks, and advanced packaging slots — a system-level allocation problem, not a lithography one.
layers.concentration: Merchant accelerators highly concentrated in one vendor; custom-ASIC design partners concentrated in two US-listed houses. The scarcity has migrated downstream of the design layer.

candidates.role: merchant accelerator incumbent; the demand signal the whole chain reads off
candidates.note: End-node. Attention pools here, so it is the least mispriced point on the chain — held as a reference, not a discovery.

candidates.role: second merchant accelerator; also the server-CPU side of the same rack
custom XPU design partner + networking silicon; captures ASIC economics without fab risk
the other custom-ASIC house; optical DSP and interconnect silicon

layers.watch_signal: Hyperscaler capex direction (pipeline `macro`), and whether accelerator lead times compress while packaging lead times do not — that divergence is the tell that the bottleneck has fully migrated.

layers.name: Server CPU
layers.bottleneck_mechanism: Inference and agentic workloads raise CPU-per-rack demand while advanced process and packaging capacity is allocated to accelerators first, extending CPU lead times.
layers.concentration: Effectively a duopoly in x86 plus an emerging Arm-based custom tier at the hyperscalers.

candidates.role: x86 server CPU + a US-located leading-edge fab footprint
candidates.note: Spans two layers — read the fab-jurisdiction layer too.

candidates.role: x86 server CPU share gainer
the IP the hyperscalers' custom server CPUs are built on
candidates.note: Royalty model — captures the shift to custom CPUs regardless of who wins it.

layers.watch_signal: Published server-CPU lead times and allocation commentary; a lengthening CPU lead time while GPU lead times shorten confirms the Kiwoom rung-3 claim.

layers.name: HBM / high-bandwidth memory
layers.bottleneck_mechanism: HBM consumes materially more wafer area per bit than commodity DRAM, and each stack adds TSV and bonding steps whose yield falls with stack height. Adding capacity means a fab construction cycle, not a line reconfiguration.
layers.concentration: Three suppliers worldwide, two of them Korean, one US-listed. Geographically concentrated in Korea and the US.

candidates.role: US-listed HBM producer; also commodity DRAM and NAND. 2026 HBM sold out under 3-5yr LTAs backed by ~$22B of customer prepayments — the sold-out book passes the funded test
candidates.note: Cycle caveat: from 3Q26 the same CSP LTAs contractually CAP realised pricing. Margins are at a cycle extreme.

candidates.role: SK Hynix ADS on NASDAQ — the HBM share leader, now directly US-listed
candidates.note: Listed 2026-07-10 (424B4, CIK 0002120882; 177.9M ADSs at $149.00). CORRECTION: an earlier version of this map said no US line existed, because only SKHYY/HXSCL/SKHYF were tested. **1 ADS = 1/10 common share** — a sizing trap. Adds NO diversification to a holder of the KRX line.

candidates.role: HBM4/4E BASE DIE — HBM3E used in-house base dies, HBM4E moves to TSMC N12/N3P, so three rival memory makers converge on ONE foundry for the differentiating layer
candidates.note: The bottleneck-within-the-bottleneck of the memory cluster, but heavily exposure-diluted inside TSM.

layers.name: NAND, enterprise SSD and storage
layers.bottleneck_mechanism: AI inference pulls high-capacity eSSD demand forward while NAND capacity additions were deferred through the prior downcycle; QLC high-capacity drives qualify slowly.
layers.concentration: Five-ish suppliers, two US-listed after the storage separations.

layers.name: Memory interface silicon — RCD/DB buffers, CXL controllers, HBM PHY/controller IP
layers.bottleneck_mechanism: Every server memory generation needs a standards-qualified interface chipset; qualification is slow and the standard itself limits how many implementations exist. The toll repeats on every platform regardless of which memory maker wins the socket.
layers.concentration: A very short merchant list — effectively one US-listed name plus Chinese and Korean suppliers Western platforms partly avoid.

candidates.role: merchant memory-interface chipsets plus HBM controller and PHY IP — a royalty-and-content toll on server memory rather than a bet on memory pricing
candidates.note: Surfaced by the independent Codex map as a layer the first pass missed. High gross margin, and it was among the most drawn-down names in the cohort at the pipeline run — worth resolving why.

layers.watch_signal: The bill of materials of the next server memory platform — the falsifier is the merchant interface being displaced by internal silicon.

layers.name: Yield analytics and manufacturing-data orchestration
layers.bottleneck_mechanism: Chiplet and multi-die assembly fragments manufacturing data across fab, OSAT and test houses; correlating it becomes a yield constraint in its own right. Software scales without the capital intensity of another inspection tool.
layers.concentration: A thin merchant layer competing against tool-OEM bundled analytics and in-house teams.

candidates.role: PDF Solutions — semiconductor-native data layer spanning fab, test, assembly and package
candidates.note: Added from the independent Codex map. The bear case is a fab or OSAT standardising on bundled tool-OEM analytics instead.

layers.watch_signal: Named OSAT or fab standardisation decisions — this layer is won by becoming the default workflow, and lost the same way.

layers.name: Fibre, FAUs, optical connectors and precision attach
layers.bottleneck_mechanism: Coupling light into a package at production yield is a precision-alignment problem with a lot of private know-how; connector density per rack rises with every fabric generation.
layers.concentration: Concentrated in a few private and foreign specialists, with the large US connector houses as the broad public route.

candidates.role: high-density interconnect and cable assemblies
candidates.note: Broad route only — the scarce private attach know-how is not inside it.

candidates.role: precision optical assembly at contract scale

foreign_only.name: SENKO, US Conec and other private FAU / precision-attach specialists
foreign_only.us_route: Private — no vehicle exists. Rung 4; APH is the nearest broad analog and is explicitly NOT the same economics.

layers.watch_signal: Whether optical-engine yield commentary blames alignment/attach rather than the laser — that would move this layer from constraint toward bottleneck.

layers.name: Advanced packaging — CoWoS, SoIC, EMIB, FOPLP and OSAT
layers.bottleneck_mechanism: Interposer area grows faster than reticle economics allow, so effective yield per wafer falls as GPU packages grow; 2.5D/3D capacity is added in discrete, long-lead increments.
layers.concentration: RECLASSIFIED bottleneck -> constraint on sourced evidence: the CoWoS supply/demand gap is CLOSING, from ~20% to ~10% by end-2026, as capacity goes from ~35k wpm (late-2024) to 120-140k wpm, with TSMC deliberately outsourcing ~240-270k wafers/yr to Amkor and SPIL. Capacity quadrupling and being outsourced is a fundable constraint, not physics. The durable chokepoints sit two layers below, in substrate-materials.

candidates.role: the largest US-listed OSAT; advanced packaging capacity including a US-located footprint
candidates.note: Thin gross margin is structural for OSAT — do not read it as a quality verdict.

candidates.role: owns the dominant CoWoS capacity; ADR makes it US-accessible
ASE ADR — the other large OSAT

layers.watch_signal: CoWoS capacity-expansion announcements versus accelerator unit forecasts; the shortfall percentage is the binding test.

layers.name: Advanced-packaging equipment — bonders, die attach, panel-level tools
layers.bottleneck_mechanism: Thermocompression and hybrid bonders are high-precision, long-lead tools with long customer qualification cycles; a packaging capacity add cannot outrun bonder delivery.
layers.concentration: A handful of suppliers globally, weighted to Japan, the Netherlands and Singapore. IMPORTANT — concentration here is FALLING, not rising: AMAT has invested in Besi, ASML is reportedly evaluating entry, and Korean makers are pushing in. A layer being de-monopolised should not be tagged a bottleneck on the bonder hop alone. Disclosed advanced-packaging revenue share favours the INSPECTION names over the bonder names: CAMT ~70% of Q1'26 revenue and ONTO >50% of 2026, while KLIC's packaging share is undisclosed. Inspection captures the ramp without having to pick the bonder winner.

candidates.role: bonding equipment — wire, thermocompression and fluxless; the US-listed pure-play on the packaging tool cycle
candidates.note: Revenue and margin were both inflecting sharply as of the latest pipeline run — the clearest stage-inflection in the equipment layer.

candidates.role: MOCVD, ion-beam deposition and anneal — the tools that CREATE InP laser and compound-semi capacity, one hop below the laser vendors
candidates.note: The independent Codex map reports a PENDING VECO/ACLS combination — NEEDS VERIFICATION, including which ticker survives. Do not size this name without resolving that first.

candidates.role: panel-level and packaging inspection/metrology — the tool that gates whether a packaging line can be qualified at all
candidates.note: Held by the investor. Also the named partner in glass-core LIDE work — see substrate-glass-core.

candidates.role: packaging and advanced-node inspection
candidates.note: Revenue was flat across the last five quarters in the pipeline run — the stage read separates it sharply from KLIC.

foreign_only.name: BE Semiconductor (Netherlands) — hybrid bonding, the bottleneck-within-the-bottleneck for HBM4-class 3D stacking
foreign_only.us_route: BESIY ADR — VERIFIED priceable via the pipeline on 2026-07-26. Rung 1. On the raw metrics it was growing faster and at a far higher gross margin than the US-listed packaging-equipment names, and it was drawn down comparably. This is the single most important ladder correction on the map: the best hybrid-bonding expression is accessible, and it is not a US company.

layers.name: Package substrate — FC-BGA and high-layer-count MLB
layers.bottleneck_mechanism: AI package area and I/O count force more layers and larger panels; process time and yield loss both scale with layer count, so effective capacity falls even as nominal capacity rises.
layers.concentration: FC-BGA is overwhelmingly Japanese, Korean and Taiwanese; there is no US-listed FC-BGA pure-play. High-layer MLB has one significant US-listed player.

candidates.role: high-layer-count PCB/MLB for AI compute and networking; the closest US-listed expression of the substrate squeeze
candidates.note: MLB, not FC-BGA — an adjacent layer, not the same node. Do not let the ticker stand in for FC-BGA exposure.

foreign_only.name: Ibiden, Shinko Electric (Japan), AT&S (Austria), Unimicron (Taiwan) — the actual FC-BGA suppliers
foreign_only.us_route: No usable US lines of adequate liquidity. Rung 4: leave as a map node and route capital to the equipment and materials layers that gate their expansion instead.

layers.watch_signal: FC-BGA lead times and any announced capacity expansion, which reads through to substrate-equipment and upstream-materials orders before it reads through to the substrate makers themselves.

layers.name: Glass-core substrate and glass interposer
layers.bottleneck_mechanism: Glass cores need through-glass vias drilled without micro-cracking, which is a distinct process (laser-induced deep etching) with essentially one credible tool owner, plus metrology able to inspect the vias at volume.
layers.concentration: Very high at the tool layer — a single small German company is the recognised LIDE owner; glass supply itself concentrates in a few large glassmakers.

candidates.role: metrology partner for glass-core mass production
candidates.note: The ONTO–LPKF LIDE partnership is asserted in the Serenity thesis DB, not verified against a filing this session (EDGAR blocked). Treat as DEDUCED until a company source confirms.

candidates.role: glass substrate and optical glass supply
candidates.note: Corning's glass-substrate role in semiconductor packaging is directionally established but the AI-package revenue share is unquantified here.

candidates.role: LPKF Laser & Electronics US OTC line — the LIDE tool owner
candidates.note: Micro-cap OTC. Priced on 2026-07-26 but liquidity is the binding practical constraint, not the thesis.

foreign_only.name: LPKF Laser & Electronics (Germany) — LIDE glass processing
foreign_only.us_route: LPKFF OTC line exists and prices; rung 1, with a hard liquidity caveat.

layers.watch_signal: Any named customer qualifying glass-core substrates for a production part, versus continued prototype-stage announcements — the prototype-to-production gap is where this layer's design wins historically die.

layers.name: Upstream substrate materials — CCL, T-glass, HVLP copper foil, ABF, drill bits
layers.bottleneck_mechanism: High-speed, low-loss signalling forces a thin high-spec cut of otherwise ordinary materials — low-Dk glass yarn, very-low-profile copper foil — whose qualified supplier set is far narrower than the commodity tier beneath it.
layers.concentration: SOURCED 2026-07-26: Ajinomoto Fine-Techno holds >95% of ABF film, notified a ~30% price increase for Q3-2026, and its expansion adds only ~+50% output with a third plant not producing until the 2030s. Nittobo holds ~90% of certified low-Dk T-glass cloth (~60-70% of NE-glass) with no new capacity before mid-2027. Mitsui Kinzoku holds >40% of AI-server HVLP copper foil against an industry shortfall of roughly 28%/39%/38% in 2026/27/28. Micro drills are a two-supplier duopoly (Union Tool, Topoint) where Unimicron and GCE took strategic stakes in Topoint in May-2026 — customers funding their own supplier's capacity, the replication-funding tell. This is where the high-grade-cut test bites hardest.

candidates.role: Element Solutions / MacDermid Alpha — IC-substrate and RDL via-fill copper plating chemistry, incl. seedless alkaline Cu for fine-pitch interposers; the cleanest US pick-and-shovel on the substrate layer
candidates.note: Surfaced by the packaging research agent. Not scored this session — AI-linked revenue materiality unverified.

candidates.role: Park Aerospace — low-loss laminate and dielectric materials; a partial, small-cap US-listed expression
candidates.note: WARNING: the 2026 laminate/CCL price spike is NOT purely AI demand. An April-2026 strike at SABIC's Jubail complex took offline the line supplying ~70% of electronic-grade PPE/PPO resin, with a 6-9 month recovery. Any CCL/PCB margin re-rate read as structural AI pull is partly a repairable-plant artifact that mean-reverts. Applies equally to ROG and TTMI.

candidates.role: Rogers — high-frequency laminate materials
candidates.note: Growth was low single-digit in the pipeline run; exposure to the AI substrate cut is unproven.

foreign_only.name: Ajinomoto (Japan) — ABF build-up film, effectively the standard for high-performance package substrates
foreign_only.us_route: AJNMY ADR — VERIFIED priceable on 2026-07-26. Owning the exact ABF monopoly and owning an equity that moves on it are not the same thing.

foreign_only.us_route: No usable, liquidity-verified US lines. Rung 4 — this remains the honest answer for the single tightest layer on the Kiwoom chart, and saying so is more useful than forcing a proxy.

layers.name: Optical transceivers — 800G / 1.6T pluggables
layers.bottleneck_mechanism: Scale-out bandwidth per accelerator rises faster than module output; each speed step re-qualifies the whole supply chain, and laser and DSP inputs gate module assembly.
layers.concentration: A handful of Western suppliers plus a large Chinese tier that Western hyperscalers partly exclude; the binding constraint sits upstream of assembly.

candidates.role: transceiver and laser supplier; vertically integrated into its own laser chips
candidates.note: Held by the investor. Integration into the laser layer is what separates it from pure assemblers.

candidates.role: Fabrinet — contract optical manufacturing; the assembly capacity nearly everyone else rents
candidates.note: Low gross margin is the contract-manufacturing model, not distress.

candidates.role: optical interposer platform; pre-scale

layers.watch_signal: 1.6T qualification announcements by named hyperscalers, and whether CPO commitments displace or merely supplement pluggable volume.

layers.name: Laser chips — CW, DFB, EML and external laser sources for CPO
layers.bottleneck_mechanism: CPO moves the laser off the module and onto a separately-qualified external source, and laser die output is limited by epitaxy and qualification, not by assembly capacity.
layers.concentration: SOURCED 2026-07-26: EML top-3 (Lumentum, Broadcom, Mitsubishi Electric) ~72% of revenue, top-5 ~79.5%; CW-DFB top-4 ~74% of capacity. The 1.6T shortfall in 2026 is ~10M units, attributed to EML AND optical-isolator scarcity. SECOND-ORDER ALLOCATION ACTOR, CONFIRMED: on 2026-03-02 NVIDIA invested $4B — $2B each into Lumentum and Coherent — with multi-billion purchase commitments plus future capacity-access rights, reportedly pushing non-NVDA EML lead times past 2027. Also Meta-Corning up to $6B multiyear on fibre/connectivity, and Jabil locking Sivers laser supply. NOTE: the laser layer is CPO-branch-invariant — CPO needs MORE external CW lasers, at higher power and reliability.

layers.concentration: Merchant photomask is a three-player market; blanks are a two-player Japanese duopoly.

layers.concentration: Fragmented at the commodity tier, materially tighter in the vertical-power-delivery and high-density module tier.

layers.watch_signal: SIGNAL ALREADY FIRED — this layer's step-change is DATABLE, and the earlier 'constraint' framing was wrong for the transition itself. NVIDIA published the 800VDC architecture (4->2 conversion stages, ~83%->92%+ efficiency, ~45% less copper); TI unveiled a complete reference architecture with NVIDIA at GTC 2026-03-16; Vertiv/Schneider/Eaton/Delta committed commercial product for H2-2026 timed to Kyber; named buyers designing for 800V include CoreWeave, Lambda, Nebius, Oracle Cloud and Together AI. BUT two reference designs fork — NVIDIA's own, and OCP 'Mt Diablo'/Diablo 400 co-authored by Google, Meta and Microsoft, which NVIDIA did NOT co-author. Nobody owns the standard alone, so this is an Evolution CONTENT-PER-RACK re-rate, not scarcity rent; suppliers qualified into BOTH capture the union. Tell that the device layer is not a chokepoint: NVIDIA's 800VDC silicon partner list has FOURTEEN names.

layers.name: MLCC and passives
layers.bottleneck_mechanism: GPU and CPU power density raises both the count and the capacitance of MLCCs per board, and the AI-server tier demands high-capacitance plus high-reliability parts that only a narrow qualified supplier set makes.
layers.concentration: The commodity tier is broadly supplied; the high-spec AI-server cut is a tight Japanese and Korean oligopoly. This is a high-grade-cut case — but content value per board is small, so unit growth does not automatically become supplier pricing power.

layers.watch_signal: HIGH-GRADE-CUT TEST PASSES, sourced 2026-07-26 — differential pricing is the proof: commodity high-cap MLCC +15-20% since Feb-2026 versus AI-specific grades +50-60%; Murata +15-35% effective 2026-04-01; lead times gone from 8 weeks to 20, some 26-40; high-end utilisation 90-95% with new capacity not ramping until 2027. Content is real: a GB300-class server takes ~30,000 MLCCs, a rack up to ~450,000. The commodity tier is NOT tight. DEEPEST STILL-RISING HOP sits one layer BELOW MLCC: heavy-rare-earth dopant + sub-micron BaTiO3 + high-end Ni electrode powder — heavy-RE doping is chemically required (pure BaTiO3 reacts with the Ni electrode during sintering) and >90% of high-purity heavy-RE refining is in China under active export restriction, with concentration RISING as content per rack rises ~10x. Honest US route for that hop: rung 4, map node only. MP-type light-RE/magnet names are the WRONG chain — do not substitute.

layers.concentration: Moderately concentrated; the tightest sub-nodes are large transformers and switchgear rather than the cooling equipment itself.
